text.p: Brisbane broking house Wilson HTM Ltd was recommending Australia's biggest food group Goodman Fielder Ltd as a buy investment as benefits begin to flow from a major reorganisation aimed at improving underperforming assets.
"Under managing director David Hearn, the company has undergone a major reorganisation with a focus on its core Australiasian businesses," Wilson said in an investment report.
A framework had also been implemented to improve underperforming food assets, Wilson said.
Six cost-saving projects were underway, each of which were conservatively estimated to generate at least A$5 million in earnings before interest and tax (EBIT), Wilson said.
Distribution and warehousing was the most significant, with cost savings eastimated in the "tens of milions of dollars", the report said.
"We believe Goodman Fielder is in the early stage of a three to five year period of improved performance," Wilson analysts said.
Wilson was forecasting net profit for the year ended June 30, 1977 of A$100.4 million, compared with an actual $28.5 million in 1995/96.
"The favourable impact of lower wheat costs in the (current year) second half should ensure that the company will achieve double-digit earnings growth for the full year," Wilson said.
Goodman Fielder shares were one cent lower at A$1.67 at 1.20 p.m. on Monday, compared with A$1.61 when the report was prepared.
